summary: This article explains how rainwater sinks deep underground, is heated by hot rocks, and rises again to form hot springs and geysers, including springs in Saudi Arabia.
introduce: Read the title “Hot Springs” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: the top or outside layer of something
a thin line or gap where something has split
natural things found in rocks, like salt or iron

challengeTerms.def: having to do with heat from inside the Earth
melted rock found deep under the Earth's surface
heavy for its size because it is tightly packed

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that hot springs are more interesting than ordinary lakes and rivers? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how a hot spring forms, step by step, and describe one danger or one interesting feature of hot springs.
struggling: Pre-teach surface, crack, and minerals with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses geothermal, magma, and dense to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
